plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win), which means the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value exceeds the second-highest bid) and never overpay, since I only pay the second-highest bid, not my own. There's no benefit to shading my bid up or down in this format. My value is $36, so I will bid $36.

This is a second-price auction (Vickrey-style): I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. The dominant strategy in this format is to bid exactly my true value, since bidding higher risks overpaying relative to my value if I win, and bidding lower only reduces my chances of winning without changing what I pay. With no prior history to adjust for, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others do. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid (profitable), and I don't overpay since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win. There's no benefit to shading or inflating my bid. My value is $31, so I will bid $31.
